[[File:Hermitian wavelets.svg|thumb|The Gaussian function (n=0) and its first derivatives.]]

'''Hermitian wavelets''' are a family of [[Discrete wavelet transform|discrete]] and [[Continuous wavelet transform|continuous]] [[Wavelet|wavelets]] used in the constant and discrete Hermite wavelet transforms. The <math>n^\textrm{th}</math> Hermitian wavelet is defined as the normalized <math>n^\textrm{th}</math> [[derivative]] of a [[Gaussian distribution]] for each positive <math>n</math>:<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Brackx|first1=F.|last2=De Schepper|first2=H.|last3=De Schepper|first3=N.|last4=Sommen|first4=F.|date=2008-02-01|title=Hermitian Clifford-Hermite wavelets: an alternative approach|journal=Bulletin of the Belgian Mathematical Society, Simon Stevin|volume=15|issue=1|doi=10.36045/bbms/1203692449|issn=1370-1444|doi-access=free}}</ref><math display="block">\Psi_{n}(x)=(2n)^{-\frac{n}{2}}c_{n}\operatorname{He}_{n}\left(x\right)e^{-\frac{1}{2}x^{2}}, </math>where <math>\operatorname{He}_{n}(x)</math> denotes the <math>n^\textrm{th}</math> [[Hermite polynomials|probabilist's Hermite polynomial]]. Each normalization coefficient <math>c_{n}</math> is given by <math display="block">c_{n} = \left(n^{\frac{1}{2}-n}\Gamma\left(n+\frac{1}{2}\right)\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}} = \left(n^{\frac{1}{2}-n}\sqrt{\pi}2^{-n}(2n-1)!!\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}}\quad n\in\mathbb{N}.</math> The function <math>\Psi\in L_{\rho, \mu}(-\infty, \infty)</math> is said to be an admissible Hermite wavelet if it satisfies the admissibility condition:<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2020 |title=Continuous and Discrete Wavelet Transforms Associated with Hermite Transform |url=http://etamaths.com/index.php/ijaa/article/view/2138 |journal=International Journal of Analysis and Applications |doi=10.28924/2291-8639-18-2020-531|doi-access=free }}</ref> 

<math display="block">C_\Psi = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty}{\frac{\|\hat\Psi (n)\|^2}{\|n\|}} < \infty</math>

where <math>\hat \Psi (n)</math> are the terms of the [[Hermite transform]] of <math>\Psi</math>.

The <math>n^{th}</math> Hermitian wavelet has <math>n</math>
[[Vanishing moment|vanishing moments]],
:<math>
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} x^k \Psi_n(x)\,dx = 0,
\qquad k=0,\ldots,n-1,
</math>
and is therefore insensitive to polynomial trends of degree less than <math>n</math>.
<ref>{{cite journal
 |last1=Mallat
 |first1=Stéphane
 |last2=Hwang
 |first2=Wen Liang
 |title=Singularity detection and processing with wavelets
 |journal=IEEE Transactions on Information Theory
 |volume=38
 |issue=2
 |pages=617–643
 |year=1992
 |doi=10.1109/18.119727
}}</ref>

In [[computer vision]] and [[image processing]], Gaussian derivative operators of different orders are frequently used as a [[Basis (linear algebra)|basis]] for expressing various types of visual operations; see [[scale space]] and [[N-jet]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/book/10.1002/9780470050118 |title=Wiley Encyclopedia of Computer Science and Engineering |date=2007-03-15 |publisher=Wiley |isbn=978-0-471-38393-2 |editor-last=Wah |editor-first=Benjamin W. |edition=1 |language=en |doi=10.1002/9780470050118.ecse609}}</ref>

==Examples==
The first three derivatives of the [[Gaussian function]] with <math>\mu=0,\;\sigma=1</math>:<math display="block">f(t) = \pi^{-1/4}e^{(-t^2/2)},</math>are:<math display="block">\begin{align}
            f'(t)  & = -\pi^{-1/4}te^{(-t^2/2)}, \\
                          f''(t)          & = \pi^{-1/4}(t^2 - 1)e^{(-t^2/2)},\\
f^{(3)}(t) & = \pi^{-1/4}(3t - t^3)e^{(-t^2/2)},
       \end{align}</math>and their <math>L^2</math> norms <math>\lVert f' \rVert=\sqrt{2}/2, \lVert f'' \rVert=\sqrt{3}/2, \lVert f^{(3)} \rVert= \sqrt{30}/4</math>.

Normalizing the derivatives yields three Hermitian wavelets:<math display="block">\begin{align}
\Psi_{1}(t) &= \sqrt{2}\pi^{-1/4}te^{(-t^2/2)},\\
\Psi_{2}(t) &=\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{3}\pi^{-1/4}(1-t^2)e^{(-t^2/2)},\\
\Psi_{3}(t) &= \frac{2}{15}\sqrt{30}\pi^{-1/4}(t^3 - 3t)e^{(-t^2/2)}.
\end{align}</math>
